metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast upward; reduce forecast peak values.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — cap forecast after peak or apply downward drag.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting — accelerate downward correction if sentiment shifts.
- Model underestimates true volatility when sentiment is mixed or neutral — increase forecast variance or add buffer.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., after 80+ peak), model often holds too high — apply decay factor or momentum decay rule.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to overfit recent trend — use sentiment-weighted smoothing or ignore recent extremes.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment — apply sentiment decay filter (e.g., 7-day moving average of sentiment) to dampen noise.
